sources.role: official desktop builds and YAML/config/SDL2 input implementation

paths.path: config.yml beside the EKA2L1 executable by default; the data-storage key changes the single data-root folder.
evidence: docs:EKA2L1 Wiki Using the emulator (default data beside executable and config.yml data-storage)

paths.path: config.yml selects current-keybind-profile; bindings/<profile>.yml is a YAML sequence of source.type key/mouse/controller entries with source data and guest target codes.
paths.naming: The SDL2 backend uses the SDL_NumJoysticks enumeration index as controller_id; standard buttons are 0..20 and virtual axis/trigger events use 300-series codes. These are runtime indices, not durable device identities.
evidence: docs:EKA2L1 Wiki Using the emulator (GUI Preferences)

paths.path: Inside the emulated Symbian filesystem under data/drives/c/private and data/drives/e/private (and other virtual drives as selected by the game); EKA2L1 has no separate universal save directory.
paths.naming: Symbian application/game-defined files, commonly under private/<UID> directories; preserve the complete data/drives tree.
evidence: docs:EKA2L1 Wiki Using the emulator (single data folder and drives)

paths.path: No save-state feature or state-file path is documented by the official desktop EKA2L1 documentation/source.
paths.naming: Not applicable: use game-native saves in data/drives.

paths.path: Firmware/device packages are installed from File > Install device into the data root; device ROM resources are under data/roms and the installed virtual Z drive is required for matching Symbian firmware.
paths.naming: Firmware package/ROM names are device-specific (the official docs require a repackage of the Z drive); no universal BIOS filename/checksum is published.
evidence: docs:EKA2L1 Wiki Using the emulator (Z-drive repackage and Install device)

paths.path: No external decryption key file is documented; firmware/device packages provide the required Symbian system material.
paths.naming: No external key filename or canonical checksum.

paths.path: %APPDATA%\EKA2L1\Data\config.yml in packaged builds; upstream's portable default is a data folder beside the executable and config.yml data-storage selects it.
config.yml selects current-keybind-profile and bindings/<profile>.yml stores YAML key/mouse/controller entries with target guest codes; the SDL2 enumeration index is controller_id.
paths.naming: Runtime SDL2 controller indices must be probed immediately before launch; they are not persistent physical identity.

paths.path: %APPDATA%\EKA2L1\Data\drives\c\private\ and drives\e\private\ (or the configured data root), using the emulated Symbian filesystem.
paths.naming: Game-defined files, typically private/<UID> directories; back up the full Data/drives tree.

paths.path: No official desktop save-state path/feature is documented.
%APPDATA%\EKA2L1\Data\roms plus installed device/Z-drive data; install through File > Install device.
paths.naming: Device-specific firmware/ROM package names; no universal checksum.

paths.path: The official macOS build uses the portable-style config.yml/data root (normally beside the app/executable unless data-storage is changed); upstream notes macOS builds but no separate stable user path.
evidence: docs:EKA2L1 README (macOS build availability and maintainer caveat)

paths.path: config.yml selects current-keybind-profile and bindings/<profile>.yml stores YAML key/mouse/controller entries; SDL2 enumeration indices are controller_id values.
paths.naming: Probe and verify SDL2 controller indices for the exact launch; they are runtime order rather than physical identity.

paths.path: data/drives/c/private and data/drives/e/private under the configured data root.
paths.naming: Symbian game-defined files, commonly private/<UID> directories.

paths.path: data/roms and installed device/Z-drive packages supplied through File > Install device.
paths.naming: Device-specific firmware names; no universal checksum.

linux-flatpak.reason: The upstream project publishes desktop builds/artifacts but no official Flatpak package; community wrappers are not treated as the runtime.
evidence: source:EKA2L1/EKA2L1 README (release artifacts and no official maintainer caveat)
